question: The Pratiharas who first had their capital at Bhinmal gained prominence during the rule of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagabhatta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nagabhatta I was the founder of the Pratihara dynasty and reigned around the early 8th century.
 
• He is credited with defending the western frontier of India against Arab invasions, particularly from the Umayyad Caliphate.
 
• Nagabhatta I established Bhinmal (modern-day Rajasthan) as his capital, marking the beginning of the Pratihara Empire's prominence.
 
• Under his leadership, the Pratihara dynasty began to rise as a significant power in northern India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Pratihara dynasty was an important power in northern India from the 6th to the 11th centuries.
 
• They are known for their role in protecting India from external invasions, particularly from Arab forces.
 
• The Pratiharas were known for their patronage of art and architecture, contributing significantly to the cultural heritage of India.
 
 
 
• **Bhinmal:**
 
 
• Bhinmal, also known as Srimal, was an ancient city located in the present-day Jalore district of Rajasthan.
 
• It served as the early capital of the Pratihara dynasty before they moved their capital to Kannauj.
 
• Bhinmal was a center of learning and culture, producing notable scholars like Brahmagupta.
 
 
 
• **Umayyad Caliphate:**
 
 
• The Umayyad Caliphate was the second of the four major caliphates established after the death of Muhammad.
 
• Under the Umayyads, the Muslim empire expanded rapidly, and their incursions reached into the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The Pratiharas, under Nagabhatta I, were able to resist these invasions and establish themselves as a formidable power.
